title: Regular-module scalar comparison in a monoidal coefficient diagram
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be braided monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category, det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport]. Assume that $\mathcal E$ has coequalizers and that tensoring on either side preserves colimits. Let $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ and $F:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be strong monoidal functors [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], with unit comparisons $\varepsilon_P,\varepsilon_Q,\varepsilon_F$. Supply a monoidal natural isomorphism $c:F\circ P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$, meaning a natural isomorphism compatible with the unit and tensor comparisons. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring object [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Give $R=P\Lambda$, $T=F(R)$ and $S=Q\Lambda$ their transported ring structures [def-sfb-modobj-transport], and assume that $R,T,S$ are commutative. Put $\alpha=c_\Lambda:T\xrightarrow{\sim}S$, a ring isomorphism, and $H=\operatorname{Ext}_\alpha\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(F):\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Mod}_S(\mathcal E)$ [def-sfb-modobj-extension, sk-def-sfb-module-objects].
For every $a:\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}\to\Lambda$, put $a_R=P(a)\varepsilon_P$ and $a_S=Q(a)\varepsilon_Q$. For a ring object $Z$ and $b:\mathbf1\to Z$, write $t_b=\mu_Z\circ(b\otimes1_Z)\circ\lambda_Z^{-1}:Z\to Z$, where $\lambda$ is the left unitor. These multiplication maps are endomorphisms of the corresponding regular modules when $Z$ is commutative.
Then $P(t_a)=t_{a_R}$, $Q(t_a)=t_{a_S}$ and $\alpha\circ F(t_{a_R})=t_{a_S}\circ\alpha$. Transport identifies $\operatorname{mapMod}(F)(R)$ with the regular $T$-module by the identity on the underlying object. There is a canonical $S$-module isomorphism $e:H(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}S$. Under $H(R)=S\otimes_T T$, with balancing coequalizer map $q:S\otimes T\to S\otimes_T T$, it is specified by
$$e\circ q=\mu_S\circ(1_S\otimes\alpha),\qquad e^{-1}=q\circ(1_S\otimes\eta_T)\circ\rho_S^{-1},$$
where $\eta_T$ is the ring unit and $\rho_S$ the ambient right unitor. For every $a$ as above, this same isomorphism satisfies
$$e\circ H(t_{a_R})=t_{a_S}\circ e.$$
All equalities involving $q$ are equalities of morphisms in $\mathcal E$, without an assumption that sections of a sheafified tensor product are pure tensors.

source.place: Monoidal natural isomorphism F P ≅ Q; abstract coefficient-diagram form of the regular-module scalar argument required by the Constructible complexes paragraph of det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback

proof.text:
First check the asserted module endomorphisms. For any one of the commutative ring objects $Z=\Lambda,R,T,S$ and $b:\mathbf1\to Z$, braiding naturality [lem-sfb-braiding-naturality] gives
$$\beta_{Z,Z}(1_Z\otimes b)=(b\otimes1_Z)\beta_{Z,\mathbf1}.$$
By [lem-sfb-braiding-unitors], $\lambda_Z\beta_{Z,\mathbf1}=\rho_Z$. Composing these equalities with $\mu_Z$, and using $\mu_Z\beta_{Z,Z}=\mu_Z$ from [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], yields
$$t_b=\mu_Z(1_Z\otimes b)\rho_Z^{-1}.$$
Write $A$ for the ambient associator. Associativity now gives the equality of maps $Z\otimes Z\to Z$
$$t_b\mu_Z=\mu_Z(\mu_Z\otimes b)\rho_{Z\otimes Z}^{-1}
=\mu_Z(1_Z\otimes\mu_Z)A_{Z,Z,Z}(1_{Z\otimes Z}\otimes b)\rho_{Z\otimes Z}^{-1}
=\mu_Z(1_Z\otimes t_b).$$
The first equality is naturality of $\rho^{-1}$, and the last is naturality of $A$ together with the structural unit identifications of [lem-coef-monoidal-structural-coherence]. This is exactly regular-module linearity in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. All these are morphism identities, using no elements or sections.

source.place: Tag 0HAY, lemma-monoidal-coherence; direct calculation with the ring-object axioms and braiding identities

proof.text:
Let $G$ stand for $P$ or $Q$, and write $u^G_{X,Y}$ for its tensor comparison. The left unit coherence in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], solved for the inverse unitor, reads
$$G(\lambda_Z^{-1})=u^G_{\mathbf1,Z}(\varepsilon_G\otimes1_{GZ})\lambda_{GZ}^{-1}.$$
Using the tensorator naturality from that same definition and the transported multiplication of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], compute
$$\begin{aligned}
G(t_b)&=G(\mu_Z)G(b\otimes1_Z)u^G_{\mathbf1,Z}(\varepsilon_G\otimes1_{GZ})\lambda_{GZ}^{-1}\\
&=G(\mu_Z)u^G_{Z,Z}(G(b)\otimes1_{GZ})(\varepsilon_G\otimes1_{GZ})\lambda_{GZ}^{-1}\\
&=\mu_{GZ}((G(b)\varepsilon_G)\otimes1_{GZ})\lambda_{GZ}^{-1}=t_{G(b)\varepsilon_G}.
\end{aligned}$$
Taking $Z=\Lambda$, $b=a$ proves $P(t_a)=t_{a_R}$ and $Q(t_a)=t_{a_S}$. This computation needs strong monoidality, not preservation of the braiding.

source.place: Tag 0FFL, definition-functor-monoidal-categories, tensorator naturality and unit coherence; agent calculation with chosen unit comparisons

proof.text:
The composite $FP$ has the sequentially transported ring structure, and clause 3 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport] applied to the given monoidal natural isomorphism $c$ makes $\alpha=c_\Lambda$ a ring isomorphism. Naturality of $c$ at the ambient morphism $t_a:\Lambda\to\Lambda$ is
$$\alpha F(P(t_a))=Q(t_a)\alpha.$$
Substituting the two equalities from step 2 gives $\alpha F(t_{a_R})=t_{a_S}\alpha$. Naturality here concerns the underlying categories; $t_a$ need not be a morphism of ring objects.

source.place: Last paragraph: the comparison is a monoidal natural isomorphism; naturality evaluated at scalar multiplication

proof.text: The regular $R$-module has action $\mu_R$, by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. By the formula in [def-sfb-modobj-transport], its image under $\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ has underlying object $F(R)=T$ and action $F(\mu_R)u^F_{R,R}=\mu_T$. Thus the identity of $T$ is the claimed identification with the regular $T$-module. On the scalar endomorphism the transported map is exactly $F(t_{a_R})$, since the transport commutes with the forgetful functors.

source.place: Displayed action formula, applied to the regular module, and final sentence on the forgetful functors

proof.text:
Use [def-sfb-modobj-extension] with the ring map $\alpha:T\to S$. Its statement supplies the $S$-$T$-bimodule $S$, with left action $\mu_S$ and right action $r=\mu_S(1_S\otimes\alpha)$. The hypotheses hold: $T$ is commutative, and $\mathcal E$ has the required coequalizers and tensor preservation. Step 4 identifies $H(R)$ with the displayed relative tensor $S\otimes_TT$, with the same balancing arrows and left $S$-action as in that construction. Apply [lem-sfb-mixed-bimodule-right-unitor] to this bimodule and the regular $T$-$T$-bimodule. Its $S$-linear isomorphism $e$ and inverse are exactly
$$e q=r=\mu_S(1_S\otimes\alpha),\qquad e^{-1}=q(1_S\otimes\eta_T)\rho_S^{-1}.$$
The cited lemma allows different left and right coefficient rings, so no identification $S=T$ is made.

source.place: Balancing coequalizer, applied to the regular module; mixed-bimodule right-unit formula as in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Bimod.lean:685-690,764

proof.text:
Set $v=F(t_{a_R})$ and $w=t_{a_S}$. The induced-map clause of [def-sfb-modobj-extension], together with step 4, gives $H(t_{a_R})q=q(1_S\otimes v)$. Therefore, as maps $S\otimes T\to S$,
$$\begin{aligned}
eH(t_{a_R})q&=e q(1_S\otimes v)=\mu_S(1_S\otimes\alpha v)\\
&=\mu_S(1_S\otimes w\alpha)
=\mu_S(1_S\otimes w)(1_S\otimes\alpha)\\
&=w\mu_S(1_S\otimes\alpha)=weq.
\end{aligned}$$
The third equality uses step 3; the penultimate uses the $S$-linearity $\mu_S(1_S\otimes w)=w\mu_S$ proved in step 1. A coequalizer map is epimorphic directly by the uniqueness clause of the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: two maps whose composites with $q$ coincide factor the same coequalizing cocone, and hence coincide. Cancelling $q$ proves $eH(t_{a_R})=t_{a_S}e$. Every calculation is in $\mathcal E$, so in a sheaf category it does not assert that sections of a sheafified tensor product are pure tensors.

source.place: Final induced-map clause; coequalizer universal property; explicit scalar intertwining after the balancing projection
